images.caption: Figure 1:Motivation: scene structure as a prediction target.(a) OmniDreams conditions RGB video generation on schematic views rendered from external road geometry and future vehicle states. (b) BirdDreams jointly generates perspective and schematic BEV videos, predicting scene structure and surrounding-vehicle motion without HD-map or layout inputs at inference. Schematic BEV targets supervise vehicle motion during training, while the predicted BEV provides a geometric interface for ego-trajectory control.

Figure 2:Overview of BirdDreams.Two causal video diffusion transformers jointly generate perspective and schematic bird’s-eye-view (BEV) videos from an initial camera image, with joint attention over tokens from both streams. Noise levels are sampled independently across streams during training. For ego-action conditioning, the latest predicted BEV frame is reprojected along the input ego trajectory to form a soft condition for the BEV branch. Joint attention conveys this condition to the perspective branch, and cached history supports generation of successive chunks. The VAE encoder and decoder are omitted for clarity.

Figure 3:Flexible conditioning.We show example rollouts from an initial RGB frame (a) and an initial BEV frame (b), generating both perspective and BEV videos in each case. In (c), we generate BEV video conditioned on a full RGB video.

Figure 5:Reactive behavior with and without ego-action conditioning.(a) Without ego-action conditioning, the ego and surrounding vehicles respond to one another. (b) In both examples with ego-action conditioning, the ego follows the input trajectory while surrounding vehicles react to its motion.

Figure 6:Surrounding-vehicle behavior under counterfactual ego actions.We compare HD-map-conditioned variants of OmniDreams and BirdDreams using the same initial observations, without surrounding-vehicle-state conditions. The schematics summarize vehicle motion, with faded-to-solid symbols indicating earlier-to-later positions and solid arrows showing motion directions. Compared with the OmniDreams baseline, BirdDreams generates more realistic driving maneuvers while maintaining spatially coherent vehicle motion over time.

Figure 7:Diverse futures from the same initial observation and ego action.We show RGB and BEV rollouts from BirdDreams (HDMap) to examine surrounding-vehicle responses to counterfactual ego actions that may lead to collisions. Each pair uses the same initial RGB observation, counterfactual ego trajectory, and static road geometry, but different random seeds. Different surrounding-vehicle motions yield a collision in one rollout and no collision in the other.

Figure 11:Scenario editing in BEV.The schematic top view makes it easy to customize driving scenarios by adding vehicles and adjusting their positions and headings. BirdDreams then jointly generates perspective and BEV videos from this initial layout, synthesizing scene appearance and subsequent vehicle motion without requiring a corresponding perspective image.
